sections.h2: What should a seller know about Kankakee County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Kankakee County lies south of Will County along the Kankakee River, with the city of Kankakee as both county seat and largest city. The Illinois legislature created it in February 1853 from the north part of Iroquois County and the south part of Will County, and it covers 681 square miles. It also borders Indiana to the northeast and east, with Lake County and Newton County across the line.

Only two cities sit in the county, Kankakee and Momence, so most Kankakee County homes are in villages, townships and rural areas. The county is divided into seventeen townships, and the county publishes a directory of township assessors. Most valuation work happens at the township level, so the number on a Kankakee County tax bill starts with a township valuation. The Census Bureau counted 107,502 residents in 2020 and estimates 105,525 for July 2025, a decline of 2.0 percent from the April 2020 estimates base.

sections.h2: Which Kankakee County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Four bodies matter: the township assessor, the Supervisor of Assessments, the County Treasurer and the Board of Review. The Supervisor of Assessments and the Treasurer both work from 189 East Court Street in Kankakee, IL 60901.

Kankakee County property tax offices (sources: county Supervisor of Assessments, Board of Review and Treasurer pages)
OfficeRoleContact
Township assessorsValuation of each parcelDirectory on the Supervisor of Assessments page
Supervisor of AssessmentsHomestead exemptions, parcel roll, transfer declarations, equalization, notice of assessment changes(815) 937-2945, weekdays
Board of ReviewAppeals, non-homestead exemption recommendations, omitted propertyThrough the Supervisor of Assessments, who serves as its clerk
County TreasurerBilling and collection(815) 937-2960, weekdays

The treasurer's site says the office manages about 55,760 property accounts and about $257 million in annual collections, and it has Spanish-speaking staff at the counter. The Board of Review decides the assessed value of an appealed parcel from evidence presented at a public hearing.

sections.h2: When are Kankakee County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The 2026 bills were payable in two installments, the first due June 25, 2026 and the second due September 3, 2026. Taxes in each bill relate to the previous assessment year, so the bills payable in 2026 were based on finalized 2025 assessed values.

Late payments carry a penalty of 1.5 percent per month, which matches 35 ILCS 200/21-15 for a county with fewer than 3,000,000 residents. The treasurer's calendar adds a deadline for paying by personal check without a newspaper publication fee, a mailing of delinquent notices, and a last day to pay in the office, and it states that the annual tax sale for delinquent properties takes place in November each year. Ask the treasurer for the exact dates before you rely on a payment window.

sections.h2: Is there a way to spread out Kankakee County tax payments?
sections.html:
Yes. The treasurer runs a voluntary program called CHOICES that lets an owner prepay on a weekly or monthly schedule instead of waiting for the two due dates. It is meant for owners without mortgage escrow, and there is no penalty if a planned payment is skipped.

Fees for the program are $1 per electronic check and 2.25 percent plus $1.50 for credit cards. Payments can be made online, by mail, or in person at the treasurer's office or its drop box, but not at a bank. The program does not stop the 1.5 percent monthly charge on any balance left after a due date, and the full installment must be paid by each date to avoid interest. There is no discount for paying early. Anyone who sells a house mid-year should ask the treasurer how prepayments will be applied to the current bill.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Kankakee County assessment?
sections.html:
File an assessment appeal with the Kankakee County Board of Review on the county's 2026 Assessment Appeal Form, after speaking to your township assessor. The Supervisor of Assessments page lists the 2026 publication and appeal deadline dates, the Board of Review rules and procedures, and the form itself.

The Board of Review rules and procedures are posted on the same page. The board decides the assessed value of any appealed parcel based on the evidence presented at a public hearing. Deadlines run from the publication date of each township's assessment changes, which differ across the county's seventeen townships, so look up your township before you plan. Ask the Supervisor of Assessments at (815) 937-2945 for the date that applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: Which exemptions does Kankakee County list?
sections.html:
The Supervisor of Assessments office lists applications for homestead relief, and the Treasurer's calendar says exemptions must be filed by March 1 each year. Senior and disability exemptions are handled through the assessor.

  • General and Senior Homestead Exemptions, with a combined application.
  • Senior Assessment Freeze, form PTAX-340, with separate forms for the 2025 bill payable in 2026 and the 2026 bill payable in 2027.
  • Disabled Person (PTAX-343) and the Physician's Statement (PTAX-343-A), plus an application for a Disabled Person ID Card.
  • Disabled Veteran (PTAX-342) and Returning Veterans exemptions.
  • Homestead Improvements, for added value from a new improvement.

Dollar limits for each program are on the county forms, so open the form for the exemption you want before you count on a reduction.

sections.h2: What did the March 2026 storm change for Kankakee County owners?
sections.html:
Homes damaged in the March 10, 2026 storm can be reviewed by the assessor, but no storm reduction could be applied to the 2026 bills. The county explained that bills payable in June and September 2026 were based on 2025 assessed values, which reflect the 2025 calendar year.

Owners with storm damage, or a home that is uninhabitable, should contact the township assessor or the Supervisor of Assessments so the property is reviewed for the 2026 tax year. The Natural Disaster Homestead Exemption under 35 ILCS 200/15-173 may apply after the structure is rebuilt. The county lists these requirements:

  • The structure must be rebuilt within two years of the disaster.
  • The rebuilt square footage may not exceed 110 percent of the original.
  • The first application is due no later than the first taxable year after the rebuild.
  • The exemption must be applied for each year.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Kankakee County homes?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024 the typical Kankakee County owner-occupied home was valued at $192,600, and owners live in 69.9 percent of homes. Median gross rent is $1,097, and median household income is $71,281. The county has 45,655 housing units and 40,996 households.

Monthly owner costs are $1,649 with a mortgage and $718 without. The county issued 113 building permits in 2025. Some 20.3 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 92.5 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. Anyone selling a home with deferred repairs or storm damage should check the taxes owed and the exemptions in place first.

sections.h2: What local landmarks affect a sale in Kankakee County?
sections.html:
Olivet Nazarene University and Kankakee Community College sit in the county, and the Kankakee Amtrak station carries the Illini and Saluki trains to Carbondale and the City of New Orleans. The Greater Kankakee Airport serves the county, and River Valley Metro runs local transit in the city while SHOW Bus covers Momence and rural areas.

Winters are cold, with a January average low of 12 degrees and a record low of minus 29 recorded in January 1985. Summers average highs of 86 degrees in July.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Kankakee County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the County Treasurer at 189 East Court Street in Kankakee, phone (815) 937-2960. The counter is open on weekdays, and the treasurer's site shows the payment season.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for late Kankakee County property tax?
faqs.a: Late installments accrue interest at 1.5 percent per month. Taxes still owing at the annual November tax sale can be offered at that sale.

faqs.q: How do I get a senior or disability exemption in Kankakee County?
faqs.a: Apply through the Supervisor of Assessments at (815) 937-2945. The treasurer's calendar says exemption filings are due by March 1 each year, and the county posts the senior, disabled person and veteran forms.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Kankakee County assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. Speak to your township assessor first, then file the county's assessment appeal form with the Board of Review within the deadline listed for your township.

faqs.q: Is there help with storm damage on my Kankakee County house?
faqs.a: Contact your township assessor or the Supervisor of Assessments so the property can be reviewed for the 2026 tax year. The natural disaster exemption may apply once the home is rebuilt, within two years and no more than 110 percent of the original size.
